title: Architecture: orchestrator as a lazy, weighted context router (compact+pointers, anchored depth, weighted context edges)
summary: Design crystallized across a design dialogue (2026-06-09). Goal: the orchestrator returns RELEVANT context with minimal resident-context cost, because the v2 benchmark showed cost is dominated by cache_read (context re-attended every turn) — so the lever is keeping resident context small + relevant. THESIS: the orchestrator is a navigable associative memory, queried lazily on TWO axes. (1) DETAIL axis = compact payloads + POINTERS: get_learnings(compact) returns a small index where each entry carries its key; agent expands a specific item via get_task_detail(key) only if needed. (compact mode BUILT, T11.) (2) REACH axis = ANCHORED, depth-bounded traversal: today get_learnings is workspace-GLOBAL + recency-capped (top-25 verdicts/failures/recent, NO anchor, NO depth) — VERIFIED. It should instead anchor on the current task-node and return learnings within its dependency/context neighborhood. The depth machinery already exists for deps (get_dependency_tree(task_key, depth), get_adjacent) — get_learnings just ignores it. KEY DESIGN DECISIONS from the dialogue: (#1) every task/arm becomes a NODE so findings are recorded AND it has an anchor. (#2) hybrid distance+relevance. (#3) dependency-wiring is currently a MANUAL norm (suggest_links only RETURNS lexical label+summary-overlap matches; agent manually add_dependency; NOT enforced/auto) — make it reliable: auto-wire context edges on create; the wiring IS the relevance check front-loaded to creation, so a genuinely-novel task (no matches) correctly yields empty learnings, no query-time fallback needed. (#4) edges carry a scalar WEIGHT (relevance) → the dep/context graph becomes a weighted associative net; seed weights for FREE from the suggest_links score we currently DISCARD; spreading-activation-with-decay replaces the arbitrary depth=N cutoff and dissolves distance≠relevance; later, Hebbian REINFORCEMENT (bump edges whose context proved useful) makes it learn — but that needs a credit-assignment signal (the hard part,
